title: Finite-level derived tensor has constructible cohomology without a boundedness claim
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Work on the small pro-etale site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. Let $K,L\in D^b_c(T,A)$ in the intrinsic finite-torsion sense of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For every integer $i$, the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L L)$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-derived-tensor] is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. No lower cohomological bound on this tensor product is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09BQ, lemma-tensor-c (specialized to bounded inputs and finite DVR quotient coefficients)

proof.text: Use the already declared finiteness theorem Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] to install Finite A. No valuation or DVR argument is reproved in this module.

Unpack [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Tag the two finite sets of nonzero cohomology degrees by a disjoint sum, so equal degrees in K and L remain separate entries. Induct on this finite list. The empty list uses the single whole-scheme stratum, including on an empty scheme. For an added cohomology sheaf choose its witnessing stratification from [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and intersect it with the induction stratification using [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection]. Its domains are actual fiber products. The immersion is the first projection followed by the original immersion; the pullback equation also identifies it with the second projection followed by the other immersion. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-finite-local-constancy-pullback] to the further inverse image along each actual projection. The proved natural isomorphism [lem-pur-proetale-constant-module-pullback-composition] identifies each iterated restriction with restriction along its composite immersion. Transport local models by the localized restriction functor, and finite geometric stalks by the explicit stalk colimit-module functor, along these isomorphisms. This proves finite local constancy of every nonzero input cohomology on one common finite positive-length partition, without any descent along a universal homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 095I, common stratification; actual fiber-product domains

proof.text: Each finite set of nonzero input cohomology degrees is bounded above in the integers. Choose such an upper bound for each input. If a degree lies above the bound, its cohomology is zero by contradiction with membership in the finite support. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-constant-module-pullback-homology] for every stratum immersion to obtain upper cohomological bounds for the termwise restrictions.

Fix the desired output degree i. On every stratum apply [lem-pur-proetale-restricted-tensor-finite-local-constancy] to the original K-flat resolution, the upper bounds from the preceding step, and the finite local constancy statements of the tagged nonzero cohomology sheaves. The same finite stratification now satisfies exactly both clauses of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] for the degree-i tensor cohomology. No lower bound or finite Tor amplitude is inferred.
